title: WHAT IF YOU HIT AN ASTEROID AT 14,000 MPH?

segments.line: You are flying at fourteen thousand miles an hour.
There are no brakes. Only a rock.
You are NASA's DART. Five hundred eighty kilograms.
Your target is a moon, one hundred fifty-one metres wide.
You hit it on purpose, on the twenty-sixth of September.
And that shoved the moon's orbit shorter by thirty-three minutes.
First time humans moved an asteroid's orbit.
Now Europe's Hera is there, looking at the crash site.
It just found a side of Didymos nobody has seen.
Boulders. Craters. Grooves. Maybe scars from your crash.
That is how we learn to push a killer rock away.
Full film on the channel. Tomorrow: what if you flew into the Sun?
